analysis:
The PR only touches docs/reference/configuration.md. It adds a 'Prompt preparation and admission' section (head lines 587-596) documenting five DARKBLOOM_TTFT_* variables: PROMPT_CACHE, PROMPT_CACHE_MB, PROMPT_CACHE_VERIFY, TEMPLATE_LOOPS and COLD_LOAD_RELEASE. No code is changed, so there is no direct security regression. I checked the documented behavior against the threat model and found no inconsistency.

Prompt token cache (relevant to T-041, A-001, TB-007): it reuses token IDs of rendered chat-template pieces 'already seen in the request's prefix-cache scope'. The doc says the global DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE disable also turns it off. It is in-memory per tokenizer, with a 32 MiB default. T-041 covers only the prefix KV cache and its TTFT oracle and disk artifacts. A token-piece cache adds a possible new timing or sharing side channel only if its scope is not per-account. The doc claims it is scoped to the prefix-cache scope, which is coordinator-authored from account and model build. That claim is unverifiable here because the implementation, PromptTokenCache.swift, is not supplied. Nothing is persisted to disk according to the doc, so the T-041 at-rest leak #2 is not affected.

Other controls: the verify interval is a background comparison that disables reuse on mismatch, a fail-safe design. TEMPLATE_LOOPS only operates when the load-time comparison passes. COLD_LOAD_RELEASE lets later coordinator events overtake a request waiting for model load. That is an ordering change in ProviderLoop+WorkFIFO.swift, outside the supplied evidence. It could interact with cancel or authorization-grant ordering (T-010, T-053), and the next pass should verify that grant, revocation and cancel events are still applied correctly when they overtake a loading request.

The documentation states that all five variables are forwarded by LaunchAgent. That expands the passthrough allowlist, which is a code change not visible in this unit. The doc line 'Forwarded by LaunchAgent' conflicts with nothing in the base text. The surrounding section says the controls do not enable caches or alter attestation policy.

I recorded no findings. A reviewer of the code PR should confirm cache scoping and the work-FIFO ordering semantics.
